Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D levels were not associated with a diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
Sentence: "Vitamin D levels were not associated with diagnoses of major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder."
Measured as: MINI diagnosis of major depressive disorder
Population: Pregnant women from Michigan at risk for depression (by EPDS score or history of depression)
Intervention: Maternal serum vitamin D level (observational, not assigned)
Comparator: Lower vs higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 117
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational cohorts of vitamin D level against depression, but in different populations and with different depression measures, so the disagreement is genuine and most likely reflects population differences.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: 72 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors vs 117 pregnant women at risk for depression; outcome: PHQ-9 above 5 vs MINI diagnosis of major depressive disorder"}
